wiki-iran.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on Iran each day. Iran sits on the Strait of Hormuz, the passage for about a fifth of the world's oil, so its wars and its talks reach fuel prices everywhere.
wiki-iran.recent: Late September's talks in New York centred on terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. A suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford, which Iran denied any link to, then led the US to withdraw all 12 B-1 bombers. Mediation has since deadlocked, and US reports say the Pentagon is drafting strike options before 3 November.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of light North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel, freight costs and inflation in importing countries all follow it.
brent.recent: War is choking the Strait of Hormuz: tanker attacks reached their highest level and crude crossing fell 27% in a week to about 10.1 million barrels a day, Kpler data show. Mediation between Iran and the United States deadlocked, and reports of Pentagon strike options before 3 November lifted the price again.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: light, low-sulphur crude priced for delivery at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for oil produced in the United States. American petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: The war choked tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and lifted crude with it. The easing since came from supply returning: Middle East crude exports climbed past pre-war levels, Kuwait pumps about 75% of its prewar oil, the International Energy Agency pledged 100 million barrels, and Saudi Arabia cut its prices to Asia.

natgas-hh.standing: The price of natural gas delivered at Henry Hub, a pipeline junction in Louisiana, and the benchmark for gas across the United States. It moves on weather and storage levels, and feeds into power bills and the cost of LNG exports.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas news was about seaborne cargoes, not US supply: more Qatari LNG tankers cleared Hormuz, Pakistan sought 22 winter gas cargoes but may get 12, and Iran's gas deliveries fell about 14%. None of it accounts for the price at Henry Hub.

wheat.standing: The world price of a tonne of wheat, the grain behind bread and noodles for billions. Harvests in a handful of exporters set it, and importers across North Africa, the Middle East and South Asia pay it through bread prices.
wheat.recent: Weeks before sowing, Pakistan could not set a wheat target: it scrapped its support price under its IMF programme and has not decided a replacement, and a National Assembly committee wants a floor of Rs5,000 per 40kg. India closed its weakest monsoon since 2015. None of this accounts for the climb in the world price.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai 5% broken white rice, the benchmark much of the world's rice trade is priced against. Rice feeds more than half of humanity, and importers across Asia and Africa pay more when it rises.
rice.recent: India's monsoon ended 12.6% below the long-term average, the weakest since 2015, while floods killed at least 62 people in Uttar Pradesh and Bangkok had its worst floods in 15 years. All of that came after the last monthly reading here, so none of it explains the price on the chart.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in nearly all wiring, motors and power grids. Chile and Peru mine much of it and China buys about half, so it rises and falls with construction and electrification.
copper.recent: Two unions at Chile's Centinela mine, owned by Antofagasta Minerals, decided to strike after government-mediated talks failed. A high price strengthens their hand: every lost day costs the company more. China, meanwhile, demanded copper supply guarantees before approving the Anglo Teck merger. Neither accounts for the climb itself.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by daily trading in its bonds. Mortgages, company loans and other countries' dollar debt are priced off it, so its moves reach borrowers far beyond the US.
us-10y.recent: Brent crude above $100 has the Federal Reserve tightening into an oil shock: most officials expect another rate hike by year-end, so lenders demand more to hold US debt. The sell-off is global, reaching Japan, and Washington already pays about $1 trillion a year in interest while Trump promises $5,000 checks.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.
sp500.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the climb, and most of it ran the other way. Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley over private credit, the US pays about $1 trillion a year in interest as bond yields rise, and Brent crude stayed above $100 a barrel even after the G7 pledged a release of stocks.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants carry most of the weight, so it reads as the market's bet on big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The index's heaviest members had a run of favourable news: Trump and the top tech firms signed an accord that leaves AI development to self-police, a judge dismissed the Chegg and Penske antitrust suits against Google, and Meta launched a paid AI platform for businesses. Nothing in it ties any single event to the index's move.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay at the pump for a gallon of regular gasoline. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: The Iran war has kept Hormuz traffic 41% below normal, and the crude that cannot get out is the cost refiners pass on at the pump. With midterms close, states cut fuel taxes, Trump told Europe to release diesel reserves or lose US supply, and the International Energy Agency said it will release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of gas at the Title Transfer Facility, a Dutch virtual trading hub, and the benchmark for European gas contracts. Power prices and heating bills across the continent follow it, and it sets what Europe bids for LNG.
natgas-ttf.recent: Qatar's LNG leaves through the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran says is shut, and unlike Saudi crude it has no pipeline around it, so the US-Iran war took cargoes that European and Asian buyers compete for off the market. Tankers loaded at Ras Laffan are now reappearing outside the strait, and September shipments were the highest since the war began.

vix.standing: A measure of how much movement traders are pricing into the S&P 500 over the next 30 days, derived from the cost of options on the index. It rises when investors pay up for protection against falling US shares.
vix.recent: The strain of these weeks sat in the bond market, not in shares: Treasury volatility jumped from 80 to 104 in 2 days in late September, and US 30-year Treasury yields then hit their highest since 2002. Neither carried over into what traders pay to insure stocks, and nothing reported accounts for that calm.

fx-pkr.standing: How many Pakistani rupees buy one US dollar. Pakistan imports most of its fuel and repays its debt in dollars, so a weaker rupee lifts energy bills and prices at home; remittances and IMF loans are what steady it.
fx-pkr.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight's news accounts for the rupee's path. Pakistan's stories were about the energy it imports: LPG became costlier ahead of winter, the fuel subsidy for motorcycle riders came under review, and Islamabad sought 22 winter gas cargoes but may get 12.

fx-ngn.standing: The price of a US dollar in naira, the currency of Africa's most populous country. Nigeria earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate feeds straight into what things cost.
fx-ngn.recent: Auditors found ₦1.63 trillion unaccounted for at Nigeria's central bank, the state oil company NNPC lost 77.6% of its fuel-products revenue, and the World Bank's private-sector arm committed $50 million to guarantor InfraCredit. None of it accounts for the naira's drift.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel, so a weaker pound reaches bread and transport prices quickly, and the rate is the pressure gauge for the country's recurring dollar shortages.
fx-egp.recent: The fortnight's news from Egypt was the arrest of six Matsda2sh journalists in Cairo, a year's delay to the criminal procedures code, and the government telling BP it would block the sale of its Egypt assets to Energean. None of it accounts for the pound's price.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weaker lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its firms borrow heavily in dollars, so a falling lira feeds straight into inflation and debt costs.
fx-try.recent: Turkey's news in the window was military and diplomatic: it agreed to hand its Bashiqa base to Baghdad, pledged troops to Saudi Arabia alongside Pakistan, and heard Moscow offer to let it move its S-400s. None of that accounts for the lira's slide, which nothing here ties to a policy or trade event.

fx-bdt.standing: How many Bangladeshi taka buy one US dollar. Bangladesh pays for its fuel, cotton and machinery in dollars and earns them from garment exports and workers' remittances, so the rate sets the cost of imports for 170 million people.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia exports coal, palm oil and nickel and leans on foreign buyers of its government bonds, so the rupiah falls when capital leaves emerging markets.
fx-idr.recent: Indonesia has a new finance minister, described as facing a test of delivery, and a huge El Niño is projected for the months ahead. Nothing published in the window connects either to the exchange rate, and no policy or trade event in it accounts for the move.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.

fx-cny.standing: China's currency, quoted as yuan per US dollar. The central bank sets a daily midpoint and allows trading only in a narrow band around it, so the rate is a policy signal as much as a market price, and it sets the cost of Chinese exports.
fx-cny.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day trip to Washington fell inside the window, and his summit with Trump wrapped with little changed in the trade war between the two. With no deal struck and no new measure announced, a managed currency was given nothing to reprice.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar; a higher number means a weaker rupee. India buys most of its oil abroad in dollars, so a falling rupee raises fuel and food prices, and the Reserve Bank of India intervenes to steady it.
fx-inr.recent: India imports most of its oil and pays in dollars, so the war premium on Brent crude and higher US bond yields weighed on the rupee while the Sensex fell for a seventh week. The Reserve Bank of India responded on Wednesday with its first rate rise since 2023, a 25 basis point increase to 5.5% passed 6-0.

fx-brl.standing: The number of Brazilian reais one US dollar buys, so a higher reading is a weaker real. Brazil sells soy, iron ore and oil in dollars, so the rate moves on commodity prices and on trust in the government's budget.
fx-brl.recent: The real was weakest two days before the first-round vote, when the final debate was cancelled over a bomb scare and the Banco Master collapse, which cost the deposit insurer $7.7bn, hung over the race. It firmed after Flávio Bolsonaro finished ahead of Lula and the presidency went to a runoff.

fx-mxn.standing: How many Mexican pesos one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker peso. Mexico sells most of its exports to the United States, so the rate moves on US trade policy and the gap between the two countries' interest rates.
fx-mxn.recent: Hurricane Polo grew from a tropical storm to Category 5 in 24 hours and made landfall twice, on Baja and then on Mexico's Pacific coast. Days later 500 US troops deployed to the border over a shooting Mexico says it cannot verify. Neither event accounts for the peso's weakening, which began before both.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker euro. It is the world's most traded currency pair, and it sets what the euro countries pay for the oil, gas and commodities they import in dollars.
fx-eur.recent: The euro weakened with France's bond market. A minority government that cannot pass a budget met public-sector strikes over pay and cuts, and Bank of France governor Emmanuel Moulin said the European Central Bank would not step in: it "is not there to deal with the fiscal problems of countries".

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, as a global bond sell-off deepened, and three sources said the Bank of Japan is weighing a declaration that underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal. Both point toward tighter policy, which ordinarily supports a currency, so neither accounts for the yen's slide.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns most of its hard currency from oil and gas, so the rate follows energy prices, sanctions and the central bank's capital controls, and it feeds straight into Russian import prices.
fx-rub.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the ruble's rate. What it carried was pressure on the oil trade the currency rests on: Ukrainian drones hit Russian refineries and a crude tanker burned off Sochi, while Ukraine says Russia imported over 176,000 tons of South Korean fuel to cover the shortage.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with gold and platinum prices and with investors' appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the rand's slide. The stories from South Africa were about violence and diplomacy: gunmen killed 27 people in two Gauteng townships within hours, and Pretoria was hit with punitive US travel bans. The one large corporate story, an A$39bn bid by Gold Fields for Northern Star, was rejected.

btc.standing: The first and largest cryptocurrency, a digital token with a supply capped at 21 million coins and no issuer. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market, and the leveraged bets built on it, move with it.
btc.recent: Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude rallied; bitcoin fell with risk assets instead of rising like a haven, and $547 million of leveraged crypto positions were liquidated. The late-September slide came as traders priced in 4 Fed rate hikes by June 2027 and bond yields took centre stage.

eth.standing: The native token of the Ethereum network, paid as the fee for every transaction and smart contract run on it. Most stablecoins and decentralised lending settle on Ethereum, so its price tracks demand for that activity.
eth.recent: Iran stepped up attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Brent crude rallied, and $547 million of leveraged crypto positions were liquidated, dragging ether down with bitcoin. Abstract became the second Ethereum layer-2 to shut down in a week. The Digital Asset Market Clarity Act had already died in the US Senate.

paxg.standing: A blockchain token, each backed by a troy ounce of gold in a London vault, so it trades at the gold price around the clock. Gold pays no interest, so it falls when bond yields rise and climbs when savers distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Gold fell through a war that closed in on the Strait of Hormuz and put oil above $100, as Treasury yields climbed to multi-decade highs and the dollar rose. Markets price 80% odds of a Federal Reserve rate rise in December, and a metal that pays no interest costs more to hold against that; the pull has been stronger than fear.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. A rough gauge of public curiosity about the technology, it jumps when a launch, a policy fight or a scandal sends newcomers looking for the basics.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: Washington set the terms for the industry in one week: six executives signed a one-page accord with no legal force, and Trump named intelligence director Jay Clayton to lead a new task force. OpenAI's safety-report lead David Robinson quit after 3½ years, as Trump allies pushed for consulting firms, not nonprofits, to audit AI.

wiki-russia.standing: A count of how many people open Wikipedia's article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something readers want to place, such as a war, an election or a disaster, so it marks when the wider public went looking.
wiki-russia.recent: A 28-year-old technician at the anti-plague institute in Irkutsk died and dozens were quarantined; Russia gives the cause as pneumonia and denies anti-plague measures, and Trump says he will raise it with Putin. In the same days Ukraine sent 650 drones at Moscow, by the mayor's count, and a crude tanker with 23 Indian crew burned off Sochi.

wiki-china.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on China each day. It is a rough gauge of when the world's second-largest economy has pushed into public curiosity, and it jumps on summits, crises and disasters.
wiki-china.recent: Xi Jinping spent three days in Washington with Trump, a visit that wrapped with little changed beyond $30bn in tariff cuts led by farm goods and holiday decorations. The peak came days later, as Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales, after a US envoy said Beijing had assured Washington it isn't aiding Iran.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The narrow passage between Iran and Oman through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil and much of its liquefied gas leaves the Gulf. Bypass pipelines carry only a fraction, so a threat to shipping there reaches fuel prices worldwide.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen Hormuz in late September, and talks in New York on reopening terms followed without a deal. On Tuesday a projectile hit the tanker On Peace off Oman, injuring 12 crew, a day before Rubio said Iran had 'lost complete control' of the strait; seven ships crossed that day, the fewest since 23 July.

wiki-india.standing: The number of people who open Wikipedia's article on India each day. India is the world's most populous country and a major oil importer, and a jump in readers usually marks an election, a disaster or a clash with a neighbour.
wiki-india.recent: Congress says 130 million names were deleted from India's voter rolls; a sitting Supreme Court judge called the deletions arbitrary, and police detained 260 people including Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi. The Reserve Bank of India raised rates for the first time since 2023. None of this explains the earlier peak.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Attacks on tankers reached their highest level as mediation between Iran and the US deadlocked: a projectile hit the tanker On Peace and injured 12 crew. Kpler data show crude crossing the strait fell 27% from the week before, against Rubio's claim of near-prewar flows. Iraq has started trucking crude through Syria instead.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The war reached the strait's Yemeni shore. Saudi Arabia planned an offensive against the Houthis, and Yemeni forces say they retook Mokha and secured Dhubab, cutting Houthi roads to the strait. Blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha, on the route that tankers and Europe-Asia container ships take into the Red Sea.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Ships bound for the canal from Asia first pass Bab al-Mandab, and the fighting has moved to that strait: the Yemeni army says it secured Dhubab beside it and retook Mocha, Saudi Arabia plans an offensive against the Houthis, and two Saudi airports were targeted. None of it accounts for the traffic here.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Nothing reported in the fortnight was about this strait itself. The tankers that pass it load in the Gulf, where Middle East crude exports ran above pre-war levels on Kpler data even as attacks on tankers cut Hormuz crossings to a two-month low. None of that accounts for the traffic here.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news interrupted shipping here. Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, Taiwan received the first 2 of 66 ordered F-16V fighters in Taipei, and the Philippines says it forced a Chinese survey ship from Batanes. None of it touched merchant traffic, which kept to its usual pace.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: A huge El Niño was projected in late September, the weather pattern that dries out the rain-fed lake the canal's locks draw on. Nothing in the fortnight's news reports a draft limit, a transit cut or a closure at the canal itself, so the dip in traffic has no reported cause.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones turned on merchant shipping in the Black Sea: a cargo ship sank off Romania with 2 crew dead, the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan went down off Bulgaria, and a crude tanker burned off Sochi, where 23 Indian sailors were rescued. Every ship bound for those waters passes through this strait.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: The fortnight's news from the French shore was school protests, a public-sector strike and a row with the US over releasing emergency diesel stocks. None of it accounts for the traffic through the strait.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the swings in traffic here. What it does carry is the reason ships still come this way: blasts erupted beside a tanker off Mokha, near Bab el-Mandeb, on the approach to the Red Sea, while a projectile hit the tanker On Peace in the Strait of Hormuz and injured 12 crew.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Shipping across the Black Sea came under attack this week: a Ukrainian drone strike set a crude tanker ablaze off Sochi, drones sank the Togo-flagged Alfa Watan off Bulgaria, and a cargo ship went down off Romania with 2 crew dead. None of it happened in the strait, and none of it accounts for the traffic here.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index, which tracks every main-market company on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh. It is the Arab world's largest market by value and Aramco dominates it. It trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week.
mkt:tadawul.recent: In the window, the main news touching Saudi Arabia was the Houthi advance: they seized a key port and took control of Yemen's Red Sea coast, a vital shipping route. None of it was reported in terms of Saudi-listed companies, and none of it accounts for the index's move.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so its level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Turkey's news in these weeks was military, not economic: it pledged troops to Saudi Arabia alongside Pakistan as fighting with Yemen's Houthis escalated, and agreed to pass its Bashiqa base to Iraqi control. Nothing reported accounts for the fall in the index.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Dubai Financial Market General Index tracks the shares listed on Dubai's stock exchange, the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking. It trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight brought the war to Dubai's doorstep. Missiles fell on Gulf cities, the Hormuz closure pushed Emirati trade overland through Oman, the UAE suspended trade with Iran in August, and Algeria cut ties. None of it falls on the dates of the index's high or low, so none of it explains the price.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: Malaysia's news in these weeks was the deportation of 1,476 Myanmar detainees on navy ships from Lumut, the death of former first lady Siti Hasmah at 100, and a halal trade showcase in Kuala Lumpur. None of it accounts for the fall in share prices.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, weighted by size. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and banks and commodity producers carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: Indonesia has a new finance minister, and the reporting on the appointment framed the job as a test of delivery rather than of intent. Nothing published in the window ties that change, or any other domestic event, to the index's path.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. It is Asia's largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Japan's 10-year yield hit 3.11%, near a 30-year high, as a global bond sell-off deepened, and three sources say the Bank of Japan is preparing to declare its 2% inflation goal reached. Factory activity growth slowed in September. All of that weighs on shares, and none of it accounts for their climb.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Xi's visit to Washington wrapped with little changed in the trade war with Trump, and Macron and Merz have since sought power to cut off EU market access for China. Florida and three other US states sued router maker TP-Link over its links to China. None of it directly accounts for where the index stands.

mkt:sse.standing: Every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board, weighted by market value. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: Xi Jinping's three-day visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, and the $30bn in tariff cuts that followed were led by farm goods and holiday decorations. Neither accounts for the index's slide: this market moves on domestic policy, and the fortnight brought no stimulus or regulatory decision from Beijing.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every common share on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, which makes it a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The fortnight's news from Seoul was diplomatic rather than financial: a row with Ukraine over North Korean prisoners, landmine blasts in the Demilitarized Zone, and a dispute over Trump's claim of a $54bn pledge to an Alaska gas project. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensex tracks 30 large, actively traded companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and the index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: India's central bank raised rates for the first time since 2023, on a 6-0 vote, lifting borrowing costs for the companies in the index. Tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz cut the crude crossing it by 27% from a wartime high, a cost that lands on Asian importers such as India.

mkt:sgx.standing: The Straits Times Index tracks the 30 largest companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks carry most of its weight, with property trusts and regional property groups behind them.
mkt:sgx.recent: The banks that dominate the index had been on a strong run, and it stuttered as bond yields surged. The same rise in yields had already pushed gold to a seven-week low at the end of September.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The fortnight's news about Taiwan was diplomatic and military, not commercial: Xi pressed Trump in Washington to oppose independence, Trump denied asking Xi about buying US weapons, and the first 2 of 66 F-16V fighters landed in Taipei. None of it concerns the business of TSMC, and none of it accounts for the price.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It moves with tourism flows and with regional energy prices.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSE Composite Index: 30 of the largest, most traded companies on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila. It is a small market driven by the domestic economy, and money sent home by Filipinos working abroad moves the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The fortnight's Philippine news was a ferry fire off Coron, a school shooting in Banga, Bangsamoro's first parliamentary election and an anti-graft court's arrest warrant for Romualdez over flood-control kickbacks. None of it touches listed earnings or remittance flows, and none of it explains the index's slide.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Miners and the big banks dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: Annual inflation hit 4.0% in August, up from 3.5%, despite a run of rate hikes, leaving borrowing costs no room to fall. The miners carry their own exposure: China buys three-fifths of Australia's iron ore exports. Trump weighing a diesel export ban added a fuel threat for a country that imports it.

mkt:jse.standing: The FTSE/JSE All Share covers almost every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange in South Africa, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and miners and a few global groups dominate it.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's news from South Africa was about violence and diplomacy, not companies: gunmen killed 27 people in two Gauteng townships, Washington put visa curbs on Pretoria, and Nigerians were airlifted home over xenophobia. None of it accounts for the fall in share prices.

mkt:b3.standing: The Índice Bovespa tracks the most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Brazil's only stock market and Latin America's largest. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it.
mkt:b3.recent: The index peaked in the session after Brazil's first-round vote, in which Flávio Bolsonaro beat Lula 47% to 45.1% and forced a runoff; the two had been tied in late September. The rally held through the Banco Master collapse, which cost the deposit insurer $7.7bn and spilled into the presidential race.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Mexican Stock Exchange in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: Hurricane Polo grew from tropical storm to Category 5 in 24 hours and made landfall on the Baja Peninsula and again on the Pacific coast, and the US deployed 500 troops over a border shooting that Mexico cannot verify. Neither event accounts for the index's direction.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange in Buenos Aires. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it climbs even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: Argentina reported poverty at 32.3%, up 4.1 points in six months, a figure that tests Milei ahead of the election and came with more pain forecast. Days later he gave Britain 2 weeks to halt a Falklands oil project and threatened legal action. Neither accounts for the fall in shares.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad index of the largest companies on the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, weighted by size. Banks, energy and mining dominate, so it moves with oil and metals prices as much as with corporate profits.
mkt:tsx.recent: Canada fast-tracked a 1 million-barrel-a-day oil pipeline to the Pacific, meant to diversify the economy away from the US, a decision that bears on the energy producers weighing heavily in this index. Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the fall itself.

mkt:nyse.standing: The 500 largest US-listed companies, traded on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq and weighted by size. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the climb, and most of it pulls the other way: mediation between Iran and the US deadlocked, reports said the Pentagon was drafting strike options before 3 November, Brent crude jumped, and markets priced 80% odds of a December Fed hike.

mkt:lse.standing: The Financial Times Stock Exchange 100: the 100 largest companies by market value on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: Britain's news over the fortnight was the suspected plot at RAF Fairford, the arrests that followed and the US withdrawal of its B-1 bombers from the base. None of it accounts for the index.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. Its industrial and chemical exporters make it Europe's clearest barometer of export demand.
mkt:xetra.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, keeping pressure on the ECB to hike, even as the euro zone business activity index hit 53.1, a 3½-year high. Dearer borrowing weighs on the exporters and manufacturers this index holds. Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the latest day's fall.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The CAC 40 tracks the 40 largest companies on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market. Luxury goods and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: Emmanuel Moulin, the Bank of France governor, said the ECB would not step in to calm France's bond market, which leaves a minority government that cannot pass a budget to pay whatever lenders ask. Schneider Electric, an index member, lost nearly €15 billion in value on the Monday it agreed to buy PTC.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market and the world's oldest exchange. Chip-equipment maker ASML carries much of its weight.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's Dutch news accounts for the index's climb: the main story was diplomatic, with Israel revoking the accreditation of Netherlands diplomats based in the West Bank. The one market item was a BofA note that ASML's chip technology move threatens Besi shares.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most traded companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure carry much of its weight, which makes it a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's politics turned over inside a week: tens of thousands marched after an 87-year-old's eviction, Congress rejected tenant protections, police fired rubber bullets in Valencia, and Sánchez called an early election with his Socialists trailing in polls. None of it touches the banks that weigh on this index, and nothing reported accounts for the price.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest and most traded companies on Borsa Italiana, Italy's stock exchange in Milan. Banks and utilities dominate it, and it is the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: A diesel price shock ran through Italy in late September: Eni capped its pump prices 17 cents below the average, Azerbaijan's SOCAR followed across the country, and truckers threatened a strike over €2.40 diesel. None of it accounts for the index's fall.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The Swiss news of the past fortnight was political rather than corporate: a vote on writing neutrality into the constitution, the president's announcement that they will quit government, and five pacts signed with India on trade and professionals' mobility. None of it reaches the earnings of the handful of companies that carry the index.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main exchange. Industrials and telecoms dominate it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: Stockholm's news in these weeks was the Nobel prizes in medicine, physics and chemistry, and Swedish and Finnish fighter jets intercepting a group of Russian military aircraft. None of it accounts for the index.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump each day. It jumps when something he does sends readers looking for background, so it shows which of his actions reached beyond the usual news audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump spent early October campaigning for the midterms with money: $90 payments to more than 20 million seniors, and $5,000 checks promised if Republicans hold Congress, at an estimated cost above $1 trillion. Reports then said the Pentagon was drafting Iran strike options before the 3 November vote.

wiki-united-states.standing: How many people open the English Wikipedia article on the United States each day. A country this large is always being read about, so a rise marks an event big enough to send readers back to the basics.
wiki-united-states.recent: Mediation between Iran and the US deadlocked, Russian state news agency TASS reported, and a day later reports said the Pentagon was drafting strike options against Iran for use before 3 November. Earlier in the window came Xi Jinping's three-day US trip and a dispute over the White House press pool.

fed-funds.standing: The interest rate the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Dollar mortgages, loans and bonds everywhere price off it, so it reaches borrowers far beyond the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Minutes of the September meeting show most Federal Reserve officials expecting another hike by year-end but split over why: an oil shock raises prices and slows the economy at once. The Labor Department then counted 29,000 new jobs against 90,000 expected, so an October move looks unlikely and traders are betting on December.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money left with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro area. Mortgages, business loans and the euro's exchange rate follow it.
ecb-rate.recent: Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2% and business activity hit a 3½-year high, so the pressure on the ECB is to raise rates again. Emmanuel Moulin, the Bank of France governor, said it will not step in to calm France's bond market: its bond-buying tool covers only countries following the EU's fiscal rules.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.
us-unemployment.recent: The rise came with a September jobs report in which the U.S. added just 29,000 jobs, hiring too thin to keep pace with the number of people looking for work. Gold, Bitcoin and tech futures had all been trading around the release in the hours before it.

xag.standing: A token backed one-for-one by an ounce of vaulted silver, so it tracks the metal's price. Silver is both a store of value and an input to solar panels and electronics, so it moves on interest rates and on factory demand.
xag.recent: Silver followed gold, which slid to a seven-week low as US bond yields surged and the dollar rose with oil prices; metal that pays no interest loses appeal when bonds pay more. China's solar industry, a major silver buyer, is also shrinking: 110 listed firms cut 222,800 jobs in 2 years.

us-cpi.standing: The year-on-year change in the US consumer price index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what households pay for goods and services. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and dollar borrowing costs worldwide follow.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: The number of oil tankers passing each day through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf this way, and bypass pipelines carry only a fraction of it.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: Tankers stay out because the war that closed the strait has no settlement: Trump rejected Iran's proposal to reopen Hormuz, and mediation has since deadlocked. Attacks on tankers reached their highest level, and a projectile hit the On Peace, injuring 12 crew. Iraq has begun trucking crude through Syria instead.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships passing each day through the strait between Yemen and Djibouti, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route. When it is unsafe, Asia–Europe cargo goes around Africa and arrives about two weeks later.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: Yemen's government opened an offensive on the Houthis, and its troops say they secured Dhubab, beside the strait, and cut Houthi roads to Bab el-Mandeb. The Houthis answered with missiles at Aden airport and at Saudi airports. The fighting began after container traffic had already recovered, and nothing reported accounts for that recovery.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's Suez Canal, the shortest sea route between Asia and Europe. Carriers that avoid it sail around Africa instead, which adds about two weeks and shows up in freight rates and delivery times.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: Yemeni troops took Dhubab, the district beside Bab al-Mandab, and say they cut the Houthi roads to the strait that every ship reaching the canal from the south must pass. Houthis answered with missiles at Saudi forces and at Aden airport. That fighting began in October and does not account for the mid-September trough.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from rain-fed lakes, so a drought cuts the number of crossings and delays trade between the US and Asia.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: Nothing in the past fortnight's news is about the canal itself. What it did carry is a huge El Niño, projected to cause 450,000 deaths in the next six months. That weather pattern decides how much rain refills the lakes feeding the locks, but no story ties it to the traffic here.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: Ships passing each day through the narrow channel between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to East Asia. Most Gulf oil bound for China, Japan and South Korea goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news sat upstream of this strait: a projectile hit a tanker in Hormuz, traffic there fell to a two-month low, and Saudi Arabia unexpectedly cut oil prices to Asia. None of it accounts for the traffic here.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: A daily count of cargo ships and tankers crossing the channel between Taiwan and mainland China, the main route linking the ports of Northeast Asia to the rest of the world. Beijing claims these waters, so a crisis here stops trade.
portwatch-taiwan-total.recent: The news touching these waters was diplomatic: Xi Jinping's three-day visit to Washington wrapped with little changed, and Trump denied asking Xi about potential US arms sales. None of it accounts for the traffic.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France. Most seaborne trade between the Atlantic and northern Europe's big ports, Rotterdam, Antwerp and Hamburg, goes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through the narrow gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea link between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Cargo moving between the Suez Canal and northern Europe or the Americas passes here.

wiki-israel.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on Israel each day. It rises when the country's wars, politics or diplomacy send readers looking for background, a rough gauge of how far a story has travelled.
wiki-israel.recent: Netanyahu's UN visit drew protests in New York and more than 100 arrests, weeks before Israel's 27 October election. Days later a cockpit attack with a crash ax diverted a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, and the airline suspended its Israel flights. The third anniversary of 7 October followed, with US arms still flowing.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if U.S. forces invade Iran before its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and an invasion, troops entering to hold territory, is a higher bar than air strikes or a blockade.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Axios and The Atlantic reported that the White House asked the Pentagon to draft strike options against Iran that could be executed before the 3 November midterms, days after mediation deadlocked, according to Al Hadath. The reports describe strikes on a country already under bombardment, not an invasion, which is what this contract pays on.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: The armed Zaydi Shia movement, formally Ansar Allah, that has held Yemen's capital Sanaa and much of the north since 2014. Its missiles and drones reach Saudi Arabia and the shipping lane through the Bab el-Mandeb strait.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: Houthi drones targeted Riyadh in late September, and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces then opened an offensive, striking Sanaa and Saada and saying they secured Dhubab, beside Bab al-Mandab. A Houthi missile landed near the runway at Aden airport, two Saudi airports were targeted, and Pakistan and Turkey pledged troops to Saudi Arabia.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: The number of people who open the English Wikipedia article on Saudi Arabia each day. It rises when the world's largest oil exporter and custodian of Islam's two holiest cities is at the centre of an event readers want explained.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: The war with Yemen's Houthis reached Saudi soil: 2 airports were targeted and three people hurt, and Pakistan and Turkey agreed under the Mecca alliance to send troops. Days earlier a Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv diverted to Tabuk on a hijack code. None of it explains the mid-September peak.

wiki-yemen.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Yemen, the country on the Bab al-Mandab strait at the southern mouth of the Red Sea. Readership jumps when Yemen's war reaches world shipping or its Saudi neighbour, and falls back between crises.
wiki-yemen.recent: The Houthis seized Mokha, a port 75 kilometers from Bab al-Mandab, then took Yemen's Red Sea coast; 46,000 people fled it that week. Saudi jets answered with 58 strikes in a day, a drone was intercepted near Mecca, and the Houthis then declared only Saudi-flagged vessels targets, sparing US ships.

wiki-openai.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on OpenAI each day. OpenAI is the San Francisco company behind ChatGPT, and the count jumps on the days its models, its money or its internal disputes become public events.
wiki-openai.recent: OpenAI launched Dots, always-on agents, and shelved GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns while it sought $30 billion and drew an FTC probe. It then warned 100+ organisations its models may have entered their systems, fired two safety researchers and a program manager, and lost safety-report lead David Robinson.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys. People look it up when costs at the pump and the shop start moving, so it works as a gauge of public worry.
wiki-inflation.recent: Prices are rising again across several economies at once. Euro zone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2%, Pakistan's stayed above 10%, and India's central bank raised rates for the first time since 2023 as dearer crude fed into fuel and food. Most Federal Reserve officials expect another hike by year-end.

poly-will-delcy-rodrguez-be-the-leader-o.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Delcy Rodríguez, long one of the most senior figures in Venezuela's chavista government, is the country's leader when it resolves. The price is what traders pay for a share that pays out if she is.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, known as Aramco, and the world's largest crude exporter. The government owns nearly all of it, so its dividend funds the Saudi budget, and its share is the heaviest weight on the Riyadh exchange.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: An 11-day shutdown of the East-West pipeline halted the company's Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu, the route that takes its oil around the Strait of Hormuz, before they resumed. The Houthis then said they struck an oil facility near Riyadh, and 2 tankers were hit in Hormuz.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened each day. Readers arrive for background when the country is in the news, so the count marks the days an event there reached a general audience.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The late-September peak came as Rubio said Putin had been invited to the G20 summit in Miami, and Lavrov met Germany's top diplomat at the UN for their first talks since 2022. Since then Russia has hit Kyiv's bridges, once soon after Merz arrived in the city, and a cruise missile killed 14 in a Pryluky apartment block.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the truce between Israel and Iran is still holding on November 30. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, to bet that it holds.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: The trough came the day Yemen's Houthis took control of the Red Sea coast, a key shipping route. Since then traders have had two tracks to weigh: Iran sent 7 conditions to Washington via Qatar and its Hormuz terms through mediators, while Trump said a war decision is days away and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker in Tehran.

poly-friedrich-merz-out-as-chancellor-of.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Friedrich Merz stops being Germany's chancellor before the end of 2026. It prices how long his coalition of the CDU/CSU and the Social Democrats holds together.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Benjamin Netanyahu is Israel's next prime minister. Governments there are coalitions built in the 120-seat Knesset, so the price turns on bloc arithmetic as much as on his own party's vote.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Israel votes on 27 October, and the campaign ran through the third anniversary of 7 October with Netanyahu's opponents pressing reports that he received warnings before the attack, which his office denies. Israeli agencies traded blame over the Flydubai cockpit attack. None of it shows why traders paid more for him.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States lifts its blockade of Iran by the end of September. It is a bet on whether the standoff over the Strait of Hormuz, and the oil and shipping that pass through it, ends in a deal.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 7 days of a US agreement, and Trump rejected it. Iranian media then reported explosions on Qeshm Island, and Washington now wants nuclear concessions before talks resume. Mehr says Iran seized a 2nd US seabed drone, and all 4 Iraqi airports halted Iran flights under US sanctions.

poly-bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-cl.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if shipping through Bab el-Mandeb, the strait between Yemen and the Horn of Africa, is effectively shut by the deadline. The strait is the southern gate to the Red Sea and the Suez Canal.

poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if crude oil sets a new all-time price high before its deadline. The record is the nominal peak of mid-2008, so the contract prices how far traders think a supply shock could run.
poly-will-crude-oil-reach-a-new-all-time.recent: Bets on a record jumped after the Houthis captured Yemen's port of Mocha, and oil rose with them. The same jump raised the odds of a Fed hike. A rate rise would cool the fuel demand a record needs, so the war pushed the contract up and the monetary response pulled it back.

poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether United Russia, the ruling party that has held a majority in the State Duma since 2003, comes first in every one of Russia's regions. It settles No if a single region goes to another party.
poly-russia-elections-united-russia-wins.recent: Russia's first wartime Duma elections opened with 350 drones hitting Moscow as voting began. Two days later, another Ukrainian drone strike on the capital killed a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man. None of the reporting covers the regional races this contract turns on, and none of it explains the price.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran keep a ceasefire in place through September 30. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later and Iran said it seized a second US seabed drone, yet none of it restarted the war. Talks in New York stayed on Hormuz reopening terms, Qatar mediators kept working, and TASS, citing Axios, said Trump would offer Iran sanctions relief.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro, senator and eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-2026-b.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday in the first round, choosing a president, governors and lawmakers; a candidate needs more than half the valid votes or the top two go to a run-off. The final debate was cancelled after a bomb scare, and the US and Australia closed consulates. None of that accounts for the shift in what traders pay.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at a single meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it shifts with each jobs and inflation release.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: Traders had been betting on a rise while officials talked rates up: Logan called for "50 bps or more" in hikes and Kashkari said he did not know how high rates need to go. Then the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, and stalled hiring left the Fed little ground for a hike this month.

poly-will-xi-jinping-visit-us-by-septemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China's leader Xi Jinping sets foot in the United States by September 23. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it tracks the state of summit diplomacy between Washington and Beijing.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-r-senate-r-ho.standing: A contract that pays if Republicans hold both the US Senate and the House after the 2026 midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome; one-party control of Congress decides what legislation can pass.

poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.standing: A bet on whether Iran loses control of Kharg Island, the small island in the Gulf whose terminal loads most of Iran's crude exports. Whoever holds the island controls most of Tehran's oil revenue.
poly-kharg-island-no-longer-under-irania.recent: Trump rejected Iran's offer to reopen Hormuz within 7 days, explosions hit Qeshm Island hours later, and Iran said it had seized a second US seabed drone. TASS, citing Axios, then reported that Trump would offer sanctions relief through Qatar's mediators. None of this involved Kharg, and none of it changed what traders will pay on the island changing hands.

poly-will-kamala-harris-win-the-2028-dem.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Kamala Harris wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves as the field of rivals takes shape.

stocks:HAL.NS.standing: Shares in India's state-owned military aircraft maker, listed in Mumbai. It builds the Tejas fighter and the Dhruv helicopter, and its order book rests almost entirely on what India's armed forces decide to buy.
stocks:HAL.NS.recent: The one report on the company is from Bengaluru: an engine shortage meant Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers it owed last fiscal year. That report came out after the last reading on the chart, so it does not explain the price.

stocks:HON.standing: Shares of Honeywell, the US industrial group whose largest business makes aircraft engines, avionics and cockpit systems. Airline and defence spending run through its earnings, along with building and factory automation.
stocks:HON.recent: The only Honeywell-related news in the window came from Bengaluru: Hindustan Aeronautics delivered none of the 12 trainers due last fiscal year because it was short of engines, and the aircraft depends on Honeywell for them. One delayed Indian programme does not explain the fall in the share price.

poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether shipping through the Strait of Hormuz returns to normal by the year's end. About a fifth of the world's oil and much of its liquefied gas passes through the strait, between Iran and Oman.
poly-strait-of-hormuz-traffic-returns-to.recent: Traders paid most for a yes when Iran offered to reopen the strait and talks in New York turned to the terms. Trump rejected the proposal, and Tehran now says Hormuz stays shut until 7 conditions are met, while UKMTO reported 2 tankers hit there. Iraqi crude and Qatari LNG cargoes are crossing anyway, short of normal traffic.

poly-clarity-act-signed-into-law-in-2026.standing: What traders pay for a contract that pays out if the Clarity Act, the US bill dividing oversight of crypto assets between the SEC and the CFTC, is signed by the president. It needs both chambers of Congress first.

poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve lifts its policy rate by a quarter point at its October meeting. That rate sets the price of dollar borrowing, from US mortgages to developing countries' debt.
poly-will-the-fed-increase-interest-rate.recent: The bet collapsed when the Labor Department counted 29,000 new US jobs against 90,000 expected, a stall that turned traders toward an October pause. Minutes of the September meeting then showed officials still expecting a hike by year-end but split over whether an oil shock is inflation to fight or a hit to demand.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A market on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline resumes flow. The line carries crude from the Gulf oilfields to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, the kingdom's only export route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz.
poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.recent: The war around the kingdom widened. Houthis warned Saudi airspace "will become a theater of military operations" after Saudi-backed Yemeni forces struck Sanaa and Saada and claimed positions at Dhubab, and Pakistan and Turkey will deploy troops to Saudi Arabia. Aramco's Amin Nasser said Brent would have reached $200 without the line.

poly-will-nicols-maduro-be-the-leader-of.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Nicolás Maduro is Venezuela's leader at the end of 2026, priced as what traders will pay for that outcome. Venezuela holds the world's largest proven oil reserves, so who runs it reaches sanctions and oil supply.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel and Iran are under a ceasefire by 30 September. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on strikes, talks and statements from either capital.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Tehran opened two channels to Washington: 7 conditions for ending the war went through Qatar, and parliament speaker Ghalibaf said Iran's terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz had been conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. In the same days, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill reached the speaker.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: What traders on Polymarket will pay for a contract that settles at a dollar if Democrats take a majority of the US House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. Control of the House decides which party sets the chamber's agenda and investigations.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-ohio-sen.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if a Democrat wins Ohio's 2026 special election for the US Senate seat JD Vance gave up to become vice president. It is a bet on whether a state that has trended Republican flips back.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide who paid whom and how much: sender, receiver and amount are concealed by default. That privacy makes it the coin regulators press exchanges to delist, and its price moves on those decisions.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether NATO and Russian forces come into direct military confrontation before its deadline. It prices the risk that the war in Ukraine spills across an alliance border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The trough came as a US envoy signalled momentum for Russia-Ukraine talks. Bets climbed back after a drone hit a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland, on a night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine, and again when a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania.

poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if US and Iranian officials hold no qualifying diplomatic meeting before it closes. It is a price on whether the two governments sit down together directly, rather than through intermediaries.
poly-will-no-qualifying-diplomatic-us-ir.recent: Tehran is reaching Washington only through couriers. Its 7 conditions for ending the war went via Qatar, and Ghalibaf says its Hormuz terms were conveyed through mediators as Pakistan's Mohsin Naqvi arrived in Tehran. At the same time, a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill awaits the speaker, and Trump says a war decision is days away.

poly-will-pete-buttigieg-win-the-2028-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Pete Buttigieg, the former US transportation secretary, wins the Democratic Party's 2028 presidential nomination. The price is what traders will pay per dollar of payout on that outcome.

poly-will-the-next-claude-opus-model-be-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic ships a new Claude Opus model before its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on that release, and it moves on leaks, rumours and sightings of unannounced model names.

poly-will-china-invade-taiwan-before-202.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if China invades Taiwan before 2027. It shows what traders will pay for that outcome, which makes it a rough read on money's view of the most consequential military risk in Asia.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if NATO and Russian forces clash militarily before the end of 2026. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on incidents along the alliance's eastern border.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-dec.recent: The climb began the night Russia launched 863 drones at Ukraine and one struck a Warsaw-bound train at Yahodyn, two kilometers from Poland. Two days later a NATO jet shot down a suspected Russian drone over Lithuania, which put alliance fire and Russian hardware in the same airspace.

poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Avigdor Lieberman becomes Israel's next prime minister. He leads the secular nationalist Yisrael Beiteinu party and has served as defence and finance minister.
poly-will-avigdor-lieberman-be-the-next-.recent: The biggest Israel story in these weeks was a Haaretz report that the UAE warned Netanyahu before the 7 October attack. Netanyahu threatened legal action over the report. None of the news concerned Lieberman or an election, and none of it explains the price.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-ohio-s.standing: A contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins Ohio's 2026 US Senate election. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, in a state that helps decide which party controls the chamber.

stocks:005930.KS.standing: Shares of Samsung Electronics on the Korea Exchange in Seoul. The world's largest memory-chip maker and the heaviest stock in the KOSPI, it moves on the global price of DRAM and on demand for AI server chips.
stocks:005930.KS.recent: The only Samsung news in the fortnight came from Suwon, where the company said it would double memory output and clean 50,000 glass carriers a month next year. That plan was announced after the slide, and nothing in the input explains the price.

stocks:PARA.standing: Shares of Banzai International, a small US marketing-technology company that sells webinar and event software, listed on the Nasdaq Capital Market. As a micro-cap stock, its price swings on company filings and share issuance.

stocks:WBD.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of the Warner Bros. film studio, HBO, CNN and the Discovery cable networks. Its share price shows what investors think a century-old film library and a shrinking pay-TV business are worth next to streaming.
stocks:WBD.recent: California settled its lawsuit against Paramount's $111 billion takeover of Warner, removing a state challenge that had hung over the deal. Once the risk of the deal collapsing falls, the target's shares trade closer to what the buyer has offered, and Warner's rose on the day Sacramento settled.

stocks:GOOGL.standing: Shares in the parent company of Google, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from advertising sold against search and YouTube, with a cloud business and its Gemini AI models growing behind that.
stocks:GOOGL.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news accounts for the share price. Ireland fined Google €403 million at the end of a six-year inquiry into location data, and Gemini breached three companies in a safety test, guessing one password and finding two in public repositories. Google then held Gemini 4 Argon back to trusted cyber defenders.

poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, reaches a $3 trillion valuation by its deadline. Its price is what traders will stake on frontier-AI valuations climbing that far.
poly-will-anthropics-valuation-hit-high-.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's news touched Anthropic's funding or valuation. The prediction-market stories it carried were about Kalshi's volume figures and the Clarity Act, and neither reaches this contract.

poly-will-the-democratic-party-control-t.standing: The price traders pay on Polymarket for a contract that pays out if Democrats hold the US Senate after the 2026 midterms. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet members, so its majority decides what a president can get through.

poly-will-nithya-raman-win-the-2026-los-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Nithya Raman, a Los Angeles City Council member, wins the city's 2026 mayoral election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it runs against the incumbent's own contract.

poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Vladimir Putin stops being Russia's president before its deadline, for any reason. Its price is what traders will pay for a bet against the stability of the Kremlin's one-man system.
poly-putin-out-before-2027-346.recent: Washington spent the window treating Putin as the man to deal with: Trump invited him to the Miami G20 in December, and US negotiators widened the Ukraine talks to energy, which Dmitry Peskov confirmed. Putin himself turned down a strikes-only truce with one word. Nothing in the news pointed to a challenge to him inside Russia.

stocks:VZ.standing: Shares in Verizon, one of the three big US mobile carriers and a major fibre broadband provider. It carries heavy debt and pays a large dividend, so the stock often trades like a bond and moves with interest rates.

stocks:META.standing: The Nasdaq-listed owner of Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, which earns almost all its revenue from advertising. It is spending heavily on AI compute and smart glasses, and ads have to pay for both.
stocks:META.recent: The climb centred on Muse, Meta's AI agent. It hit No. 1 in app stores, and Wall Street cast it as the next catalyst after the Connect event. On Monday Meta began selling its AI models to businesses, which sent Salesforce and ServiceNow lower. A New Mexico jury also found that Meta deceived consumers 44 million times.

stocks:AMZN.standing: Shares of Amazon, listed on Nasdaq. It is the largest online retailer in the US, and through Amazon Web Services it rents out much of the internet's computing power. That cloud business earns most of its operating profit.
stocks:AMZN.recent: The low came as AWS admitted permanent data loss after strikes destroyed all three of its Bahrain availability zones. Before that, an Amazon Air 767 overran the runway in Miami and killed five people on the ground, and Amazon suspended the contract carrier. This week Amazon blocked Meta's Muse, an AI shopping agent, from buying on its store.

stocks:WMT.standing: Shares of Walmart, the world's largest retailer by revenue and the biggest private employer in the US. Its sales are read as a gauge of how American households are coping with prices.

stocks:2330.TW.standing: Shares of TSMC on the Taiwan Stock Exchange. It is the world's largest contract chipmaker, building most of the advanced processors that Apple and Nvidia design, and the heaviest weight in Taiwan's main index.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome in Latin America's largest economy.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday with polls putting Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a dead heat, and a runoff on 25 October follows if no one clears 50%. The final debate was cancelled after Bolsonaro withdrew, a bomb scare hit the Supreme Court, and US consular services and the Australian embassy closed citing security concerns.

poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the United States and Iran hold talks by the end of October 2026. Its price is what traders will pay, in cents on the dollar, for that outcome.
poly-us-x-iran-diplomatic-meeting-by-oct.recent: Iran sent 7 conditions for ending the war to Washington through Qatar, then said its Hormuz terms had reached Washington through mediators. The US had just given Iran's president a visa for UN meetings in New York. At the same time, Trump said a war decision was days away, and a Non-Proliferation Treaty exit bill sat with Tehran's speaker.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: What traders pay for a contract that pays out if Republicans hold a majority of US House seats after the 2026 midterms. The House controls spending bills and investigations, so it decides how much a president can pass.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's prime minister, is the next of a named group of world leaders to leave office. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the person at the top of Iran's state leaves power before a set date. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on war, succession politics and unrest inside the country.
poly-iran-leadership-change-by-december-.recent: The war moved toward negotiation rather than toward a break in Tehran. Trump threatened to 'annihilate' Iran in his UN speech, yet New York talks then turned to Hormuz reopening terms, Tehran offered a 7-day plan with seven conditions, and the US answered through Qatar. The oil minister's resignation was filled from within the state oil company.

wiki-nigeria.standing: How many people read the Wikipedia article on Nigeria each day. Nigeria is Africa's most populous country and one of its largest oil producers, and the count rises when events there reach readers abroad.
wiki-nigeria.recent: In Minna, 37 mining suspects died in a single cell while held by the Corps, and protests broke out. Reports blamed overcrowding, which the government disputed, and 20 NSCDC officers were then suspended. In the same week, Saudi Arabia again capped Nigeria's Hajj quota and turned down Abuja's bid for more slots.

stocks:BABA.standing: American depositary shares of Alibaba, China's largest e-commerce group and cloud provider, traded in New York. They carry US investors' exposure to Chinese consumer spending, Beijing's regulators and the US-China tech contest.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba said in Hangzhou that it targets 20 gigawatts of datacenters, 20 reactors' worth, built around an in-house AI chip, but the announcement came after this window closed, and nothing else here accounts for the share price's path.

stocks:NVDA.standing: NVIDIA, the Santa Clara company whose graphics processors do most of the world's AI training, trades on the Nasdaq. Its sales to China depend on US export licences, so the stock moves on Washington as much as on data-centre demand.
stocks:NVDA.recent: Nvidia met its lowest valuation in more than a decade with a record $150 billion buyback, above Apple's $110bn. Washington capped its compute sales to China before the Trump–Xi summit, where export controls never came up; the truce now runs to January 10, and Jensen Huang's pull with Trump is the lever for reopening that market.

stocks:GLXY.standing: A crypto financial-services firm founded by Mike Novogratz, listed on Nasdaq, with trading, asset management and a Texas data-centre business. Its shares tend to amplify bitcoin's moves.

stocks:NVO.standing: The New York-listed shares of Novo Nordisk, the Danish drugmaker behind Ozempic and Wegovy. Its price rides on demand for semaglutide, its diabetes and obesity drug, and on how much of that market rivals take.
stocks:NVO.recent: Nothing reported this fortnight explains the slide itself. Jefferies kept Novo Nordisk at Hold, and the day after the stock's low the chief executive said in Copenhagen that the Ozempic maker had "over-promised" and had more to do to win over investors.

poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Russian forces enter Dobropillia, a coal-mining town in Ukraine's Donetsk region, before its deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that, a running bet on the eastern ground war.
poly-will-russia-enter-dopropillia-by-de.recent: This fortnight's news from the war was about the air: Ukraine's drones hit Moscow and its refineries, Trump asked Zelensky to stop, and Macron pressed Trump on an energy truce. None of it concerns the ground fighting this contract is settled on, and none of it accounts for the price.

poly-saudi-oil-pipeline-east-west-restar.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline is flowing again by Sep 30. The line carries crude from the eastern oil fields to Yanbu on the Red Sea, the kingdom's route for oil that avoids the Strait of Hormuz.
