Talks in New York focused on Hormuz reopening terms; Trump rejected Iran's Hormuz proposal, and Mehr News Agency says the US has since answered Tehran's conditions. Hormuz authorities threatened to blacklist charterers, and an Iranian missile strike injured eight US Marines.

stocks:BYD.standing: A Las Vegas-based casino operator listed on the New York Stock Exchange, running regional and locals-market casinos across several US states. Its shares move with American consumer spending on leisure and gambling.

stocks:PL.standing: Shares in a San Francisco company that runs hundreds of small Earth-imaging satellites and photographs most of the planet's land every day. Governments, defence agencies, farmers and newsrooms buy the pictures.

stocks:LCID.standing: An American maker of luxury electric cars, majority-owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. It spends far more than it earns from sales, so the share price tracks how long Riyadh keeps funding it.
stocks:LCID.recent: The Saudi fund that owns Lucid is also behind a new rival electric-car maker in Riyadh, which leaves the company competing with its own shareholder's other venture. That story surfaced after the shares had already fallen and does not account for the slide.

stocks:SHEL.standing: The New York-listed shares of a London-based oil and gas major, one of the world's largest traders of liquefied natural gas. They move with crude and gas prices, and British pension funds lean on the dividend.
stocks:SHEL.recent: Advocacy outlet Declassified UK reported that Shell and BP have signed Venezuelan agreements since January, and Nigeria's attorney-general said one oil treaty dispute exposed the country to over $2 billion, a threat to cleanup after oil divestment. Neither accounts for the share price.

stocks:MU.standing: A US maker of DRAM and NAND memory chips, based in Boise, Idaho, and one of three firms that produce nearly all the world's DRAM. Its shares follow memory prices, which swing harder than the rest of the chip industry.
stocks:MU.recent: Micron says demand for memory will exceed supply for at least 2 years, a shortage that leaves chipmakers setting the price rather than buyers. The statement from Boise came after the climb, so it describes the conditions behind the move rather than the trigger for any single day.

stocks:CHGG.standing: A US online education company that sells homework help and study subscriptions to students. Its business depends on students finding it through search, which makes it one of the stocks most exposed to AI chatbots answering the question first.
stocks:CHGG.recent: A judge in Washington dismissed the antitrust suits that Chegg and Penske had brought against Google over its AI Overviews, ending the company's attempt to challenge them in court. The ruling came at the very end of the window, so it does not account for the slide that preceded it.

poly-will-anthropic-have-the-highest-ipo.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, maker of the Claude AI models, is the largest stock-market debut of 2026 by market value. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast.

wiki-united-kingdom.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the United Kingdom, a nuclear-armed state of four nations with a permanent UN Security Council seat. Surges mark the days the country itself becomes the story.
wiki-united-kingdom.recent: Police opened a counter-terror probe into a suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford, the airbase the US used for the Iran war, and made a seventh arrest, among them a British-Iranian man. Iran denied any link. The US withdrew all 12 B-1 bombers, a move the UK sees as boosting Iran and Russia. None of this dates from the mid-September peak.

poly-will-renan-santos-finish-in-third-p.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Renan Santos, a founder of the Free Brazil Movement, finishes third in the first round of Brazil's presidential election. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome.

poly-will-the-republican-party-control-t.standing: What traders on Polymarket pay for a contract that pays out if Republicans hold the US Senate after the midterm elections. The Senate confirms judges and cabinet officers, so control decides whom a president can appoint.

stocks:NST.AX.standing: One of Australia's largest gold miners, listed in Sydney and run from Perth, with mines around Kalgoorlie in Western Australia and in Alaska. Its shares are a geared bet on the gold price: costs are largely fixed, so profit swings harder than the metal.
stocks:NST.AX.recent: South Africa's Gold Fields offered A$39bn for the company, and the board in Perth turned it down. A takeover approach puts an outside buyer's valuation on the shares, and this one came from a foreign miner seeking to consolidate Australia's gold producers, so the stock traded on the bid, not on the metal alone.

stocks:GFI.standing: A Johannesburg-based gold miner with mines in South Africa, Ghana, Australia, Peru and Chile; these are its New York-listed shares. Its costs are largely fixed, so its profit and its share price swing harder than the gold price.
stocks:GFI.recent: Gold Fields offered A$39bn for Northern Star, the Perth gold miner, and was turned down. A bid that size is paid for by the buyer's own shareholders, and an acquirer's stock is usually sold when one lands. Nothing here dates the approach, so its link to the slide is unproven.

poly-will-sudans-emergency-response-room.standing: What traders will pay for a contract that pays out if the Nobel Peace Prize goes to Sudan's Emergency Response Rooms, the volunteer networks running kitchens and clinics through the civil war. The Norwegian committee decides in secret.

stocks:AAL.standing: The share price of American Airlines, the largest US carrier by passengers flown, listed on Nasdaq. Jet fuel and labour are its biggest costs and it carries heavy debt, so the stock moves on oil prices and on demand for travel.

stocks:LMT.standing: The largest US defence contractor and maker of the F-35 and F-16 fighter jets. Most of its revenue comes from the US government, and every foreign sale needs Washington's approval, so its shares follow defence budgets and arms deals.
stocks:LMT.recent: The peak came as the Trump administration approved the sale of F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia, opening a new customer for Lockheed's biggest programme. Nothing since explains the slide: the first 2 of 66 F-16V fighters Taiwan ordered landed in Taipei on Friday, a delivery against an existing order rather than new business.

stocks:TECK.standing: A Vancouver-based miner whose shares trade in New York and Toronto. Its earnings come mostly from copper and zinc, from mines in Canada, Chile and Peru, so the stock moves with the copper price and with output at those sites.
stocks:TECK.recent: China's antitrust regulator asked Anglo American to commit to a steady supply of copper concentrate as a condition for approving its $54bn merger with Teck, sources told Reuters. Beijing holds that lever because its smelters buy most of the world's concentrate. The demand came after the swings shown here and does not explain them.

poly-will-the-international-court-of-jus.standing: A contract that pays out if the International Court of Justice, the UN's top court in The Hague, is awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, set by their bets.

poly-will-lula-win-the-most-votes-in-the.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins the first round of Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Brazil goes to a runoff if no candidate clears half the valid votes.
poly-will-lula-win-the-most-votes-in-the.recent: Two days before Sunday's vote, polls put Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro in a dead heat. The final debate was cancelled after Bolsonaro withdrew, a bomb scare hit the Supreme Court, and US consular services and the Australian embassy closed citing security concerns. None of it dates to the September slide in the betting.

poly-will-indiana-enact-a-data-center-mo.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Indiana enacts a statewide pause on new data centers before 2027. Its price is what traders pay for that outcome, in a state where server farms compete with households for power and water.

poly-will-anthropic-announce-bankruptcy-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Anthropic, the AI lab behind Claude, files for bankruptcy by the end of 2027. The price is what traders pay for that outcome: a bet on whether AI revenue outruns the cost of compute.

poly-will-oklahoma-enact-a-data-center-m.standing: A contract that pays out if Oklahoma passes a law pausing new data center construction before 2027. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it turns on a state weighing power and water demand against investment.

poly-will-texas-enact-a-data-center-mora.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Texas passes a law halting new data center construction by its deadline. Texas is among the largest US sites for the AI build-out, and its isolated grid has to power it.

stocks:VIC.VN.standing: Vietnam's largest private conglomerate, listed in Ho Chi Minh City, spanning property developer Vinhomes and carmaker VinFast. It is among the heaviest weights in the VN-Index, so its share price pulls the whole market.
stocks:VIC.VN.recent: The news from Hanoi in this stretch was about power rather than this company: LNG supplies just 1.6% of Vietnam's electricity, a shortfall that stands in the way of the country's chip plan. None of it accounts for the share price.

poly-will-ohio-enact-a-data-center-morat.standing: A contract that pays out if Ohio halts new data center construction before its deadline. Central Ohio is one of the largest US clusters of server farms, and their power demand feeds into electricity bills across the state.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Nvidia authorized a record $150 billion share buyback, the largest in its history, committing cash from chip sales to retiring its own stock. Days later Trump and top tech firms signed an accord to self-police AI development, leaving the industry to set its own limits, and SpaceX followed with a big Nvidia purchase.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: A federal jury in San Diego awarded Taction Technology $5.72 billion from Apple, and the company pulled its strongest iCloud encryption from new UK users. Apple Pay launched in India on Axis Bank cards only. These are costs and limits on its business, and none of them accounts for the share's climb.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Google announced Gemini 4 Argon after months of delays and restricted it to trusted cyber defenders over safety concerns, so its most powerful model is not yet widely sold. A judge dismissed antitrust suits from Chegg and Penske, and it signed a long-term deal with Constellation Energy for 890 megawatts of nuclear output for its data centres.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Contractors were reported to be reviewing the prompts and images that Copilot users upload, and briefs were unsealed in the authors' case against Microsoft and OpenAI. Neither story accounts for the share's climb.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: Starship reached orbit for the first time on Flight 14, despite losing 1 of its 3 main Raptor engines, a failure that bears on NASA's moon mission. Days later SpaceX launched the Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station with NASA. Iran's cyberspace chief said Iran stopped Starlink operating in the war.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: The run-up centred on Meta Connect, where the company showed its Muse AI agent and camera-free Ray-Ban glasses at $349, and Wall Street took Muse as its next catalyst. Since then a Santa Fe jury found Meta deceived consumers 44 million times, and the company rushed fixes for a Muse flaw that opened a path to its internal databases.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: An 11-day pipeline shutdown stopped the company's Red Sea crude loadings at Yanbu until late September. The Houthis then said they struck an oil facility near Riyadh, with smoke seen near Aramco, and 2 tankers were hit in Hormuz. Its CEO said almost 3 billion barrels of supply were lost and replenishing stocks could take two years.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla's sales fell 2 percent in the third quarter, a result reported as underwhelming. In Fremont, workers balked at training the Optimus humanoid robots meant to replace them, and the company reportedly stopped Model S and X production in May. None of that explains the share's swings.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix together control 83% of memory chips, a hold that makes Korea a chokepoint for the AI build-out. Nothing reported about the company in these weeks accounts for the path its share took.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: Micron's chief executive said memory supplies are "only getting tighter", and the company said demand will exceed supply for at least 2 years, with AI demand behind the shortage. A maker that cannot fill its orders sells every chip it produces and sets the price on them, which is what the share reflects.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.
co:amd.recent: AMD agreed on Sep 28 to buy World Labs, the world-models startup founded by AI pioneer Fei-Fei Li, for $8.2 billion. The deal takes a chip designer into building AI models itself, not only selling the hardware they run on. The climb began weeks before the deal, and nothing else reported about the company accounts for it.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.
co:jpmorgan.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, alongside Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley, in a review spurred by worries over private credit. The review looks at what banks have lent into that market, putting a regulator's eye on a line of JPMorgan's own lending.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: Samsung and SK Hynix together control 83% of memory chips, which makes the two firms a chokepoint for AI hardware. That concentration is a standing condition rather than an event, and it does not account for the price.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: The one headline of the fortnight was about a rival's exposure, not this share: BofA said a chip technology move by ASML threatens Besi. Nothing published explains the price itself.

us-2y.standing: The interest the US government pays to borrow for two years. It follows where traders think the Federal Reserve will set rates more closely than any other maturity, and short-term loan rates worldwide move with it.
us-2y.recent: The fortnight's news carries the question rather than the answer: what Washington does next if US bond yields keep rising. Nothing in it names the cause of the climb.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders quote on a 30-year fixed home loan, surveyed weekly by Freddie Mac. It follows the 10-year Treasury yield, and it sets what American households pay to buy a home or refinance one.

ez-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in consumer prices across the countries that use the euro, as measured by Eurostat. The European Central Bank sets interest rates to hold it at 2%, so borrowing costs for the whole bloc follow it.
ez-cpi.recent: The September figure, published after this line ends, came in at 3.8%, the highest level in three years. That keeps pressure on the ECB to hike rates. The reports of the jump name no cause for it.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva finishes first in Brazil's presidential first round with a lead of 5 to 10 percentage points over the runner-up. Its price is what traders are betting, not a poll.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: Brazil votes on Sunday for a president, governors and lawmakers, and a candidate needs more than half the valid votes to avoid a run-off. Nothing reported in the past fortnight accounts for the change in what traders will pay for this margin.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The native token of the Tron blockchain, spent to pay for transactions on it. The network carries a large share of the world's dollar-stablecoin transfers, so demand for the token follows how much of that traffic runs across it.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, paid as the fee for every transaction on the network and staked to secure it. Its price tracks how much trading, lending and payment activity developers and institutions move onto the chain.
sol.recent: Alpenglow, the upgrade that cuts the time for a transaction to become final to 150 milliseconds from 12.8 seconds, reached its second public test network in late September. The Solana Foundation followed in October by launching DvP to settle institutional trades in seconds, a pitch aimed at the large trading firms the faster settlement was built for.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: Hackers stole about $350 million from the exchange Bitget on Sep 25, and it paused withdrawals. A day later the thief moved $83 million of the stolen XRP, which Ripple has no power to freeze. The same week validators reset the activation clock on an XRP Ledger upgrade, delaying it 10 days.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency started in 2013 as a joke on a Shiba Inu meme, with no cap on how many coins exist. Nothing underpins it but demand, so its price moves on attention and is a gauge of retail appetite for speculation.
doge.recent: The one development in the window was a new Ethereum-style testnet for Dogecoin, built to bring trading, lending and stablecoins to a coin that has had none of them. It is a test network, not a launch, and it does not account for the price.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that uses zero-knowledge proofs to hide a payment's sender, receiver and amount. It tests how much financial privacy exchanges and regulators will tolerate.
zec.recent: Researchers proposed Zcash-style private payments for Bitcoin without a fork, putting the coin's cryptography in front of a larger audience just before the price topped out. It gave ground as Bitcoin slipped, even as developers moved Tachyon code live, Gemini switched its Zcash software and 25-second blocks reached the public testnet early.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of independent operators that feeds outside data such as asset prices into blockchain smart contracts. Many decentralised lending apps rely on its price feeds, and LINK pays for them.
link.recent: The peak came the day after Chainlink launched CCIP 2.0, a new version of the protocol that gives big crypto apps more control over their security. Nothing else in the period's news accounts for the earlier slide or the pullback since.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: For a decade the Bank of Japan held rates near zero on the argument that underlying inflation was still short of its 2% target. Three sources told Reuters the bank is weighing saying this month that the target is roughly met, which removes its own stated reason to hold. Oil prices since the war on Iran have raised Japanese import costs.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark Chinese banks use to price most new business and household loans, published monthly under the People's Bank of China. It sets what credit costs in the world's second-largest economy.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia's published business in the past fortnight was routine: it set the official dollar rate at 83.25 rubles for October 2 and reported no yuan purchases or sales. Neither accounts for the cuts.

stocks:NSRGY.standing: The world's largest food company, based in Vevey, Switzerland, selling Nescafé, KitKat, Maggi and infant formula in nearly every country. Its sales track what households pay for groceries, and what cocoa and coffee cost.
stocks:NSRGY.recent: India's food regulator, the FSSAI, failed a sample of Nestlé dairy whitener as unsafe and substandard; Nestlé says the product is safe. The finding arrived after the last trading day shown here, so it accounts for none of the slide on the chart.

poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-first-.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro finishes first in the opening round of Brazil's presidential election with a margin under five points. Its price is what traders will pay for a narrow lead, not a forecast.
poly-will-flvio-bolsonaro-win-the-first-.recent: Brazil voted on Sunday for a president, governors and lawmakers, and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro took an early lead over President Lula as the first returns came in. Traders bought a narrow first-place finish rather than an outright win: a candidate needs more than half the valid votes, or the top two go to a run-off.

stocks:SPCX.standing: Elon Musk's rocket and satellite company. It carries most of the world's payload to orbit, flies NASA's astronauts and runs the Starlink internet constellation, so its fortunes rest on launch cadence and state contracts.
stocks:SPCX.recent: Starship reached orbit for the first time on Flight 14, despite losing one of its three main Raptor engines, a failure that raised questions for NASA's moon mission. Within days Elon Musk was named co-lead of a Pentagon study of future warfare and the company launched Crew-13 to the International Space Station.

poly-will-augusto-cury-finish-in-third-p.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the candidate Cury finishes third in the first round of Brazil's 2026 presidential election. Third place is watched because that candidate's voters are the ones the two run-off contenders must win.
poly-will-augusto-cury-finish-in-third-p.recent: The contract repriced as the count arrived. Brazil voted on Sunday for a president, governors and lawmakers, and early returns put Senator Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of President Lula, with the top two going to a run-off unless one clears half the valid votes. The published tallies name only those two, so the order behind them is what traders settled as results came in.

poly-israel-accuses-iranproxies-of-plane.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Israel formally blames Iran for a stabbing aboard a passenger aircraft before its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, not a forecast of it.
poly-israel-accuses-iranproxies-of-plane.recent: The bet follows a cockpit altercation on flydubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The UAE opened a terrorism probe and Trump vowed a tough response if Iran was linked, but Israel's own agencies then turned on each other over the co-pilot's vetting, while the US answered Iran's 7-day plan through Qatar.

poly-will-anthropics-market-cap-be-betwe.standing: A Polymarket contract on where Anthropic, the company behind the Claude AI models, is valued at the close of its first day as a public company. This bracket pays out if that figure lands between $2.25 trillion and $2.5 trillion.

wiki-terrorism.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on terrorism, the general reference page for the term. Its traffic rises when an attack, a plot or an anniversary sends people to look up what the word covers and who it is applied to.
wiki-terrorism.recent: Nothing in the news of the past fortnight accounts for the peak, which fell before any of it. Those weeks carried other cases: police bailed all five men arrested near RAF Fairford, then held a British-Iranian man, 27, while Iran denied any link, and the UAE called a flydubai cockpit attack a terrorist act planned by the co-pilot.

stocks:ICE.standing: The company that owns the New York Stock Exchange and runs the futures markets where Brent crude and other benchmarks are priced. It earns fees on trading, clearing and data, so its income rises with market volume.
stocks:ICE.recent: Two expansions landed this week: a filing with OKX for nonstop tokenized trading in 60 U.S. stocks, and the launch of gold futures in London, where nearly $190bn of gold changes hands daily without an exchange contract. Both came after the share's slide, and neither accounts for it.

stocks:PLTR.standing: A US software company whose platforms pull an organisation's scattered data into one picture for analysis and targeting. Armies, intelligence agencies and governments are its core customers, so its share trades on defence budgets.

stocks:4665.T.standing: An Osaka-based company that rents mops and mats to Japanese homes and offices through franchised door-to-door routes, and runs the Mister Donut chain in Japan. Its share tracks domestic household spending and labour costs.

stocks:1810.HK.standing: A Beijing-based maker of smartphones, connected home devices and electric cars, listed in Hong Kong. It is one of the world's largest phone sellers by volume, and most of what it ships is low-priced handsets with thin margins.
stocks:1810.HK.recent: The AI boom is squeezing the cheapest smartphones, the end of the market this company depends on. Its Redmi 15C rose 36% in India in six months, a price increase on a handset whose whole appeal is being cheap.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A prediction-market contract that pays out if the truce between the United States and Iran is still in force at its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with every strike, threat and round of talks.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Traders marked the contract down after Trump vowed a tough response if Iran was linked to the flydubai incident. They bid it back up once Washington answered Iran's 7-day plan to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, sending the reply through Qatar; deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Tehran was reviewing it.

stocks:SE.standing: The Singapore-based parent of Shopee, Southeast Asia's largest online marketplace, the games publisher Garena and the lender Monee. Its New York-listed shares are a bet on consumer spending and digital payments across the region.

stocks:PTC.standing: A Boston-based maker of the design and engineering software manufacturers use to draw products and track them through production and service. Its revenue is subscriptions from industrial firms, so it follows factory investment.
stocks:PTC.recent: France's Schneider Electric agreed on Monday to buy PTC for about $22.6 billion, the largest acquisition in its history, to build up its data-centre business. A seller of power and cooling gear is paying for the software used to plan those sites, and its own shares lost nearly €15 billion in value on the day.

poly-pedro-snchez-out-as-pm-of-spain-by-.standing: A contract that pays out if Pedro Sánchez leaves office as Spain's prime minister before the deadline. He governs in a minority coalition that needs Catalan and Basque nationalist votes, so one defection can force an election.

poly-will-the-republicans-win-the-texas-.standing: What traders pay for a contract that pays out if the Republican candidate wins the US Senate seat Texas is voting on. No Democrat has won statewide office in Texas since 1994, so a close price here is itself unusual.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A contract that pays out if Pedro Sánchez, the Socialist leader, heads Spain's next government. Spain's prime minister is chosen by a vote in Congress, so the bet turns on coalition arithmetic as much as on ballots.

stocks:MSCI.standing: A New York firm that builds the stock indices investment funds are measured against and copy. Trillions of dollars follow its decisions on which countries and companies are included, and it also sells sustainability ratings.

wiki-petroleum.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on petroleum each day. Crude oil is the feedstock for transport fuel and plastics and the world's most traded commodity, so readers arrive when supply or pump prices are disrupted.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Aramco says almost 3 billion barrels of oil supply were lost and that replenishing crude and fuel stocks would take two years. Hormuz traffic still sits 41% below normal, so Iraq trucks crude through Syria; OPEC+ kept November quotas unchanged, and the US pressed Europe to release emergency diesel stocks.

stocks:LYFT.standing: A ride-hailing company that matches passengers with drivers through its app, mostly in the United States and Canada. It is the smaller rival to Uber, so its share reads as a bet on whether a second player can hold its ground.

stocks:JPM.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, spanning consumer banking, investment banking, trading and asset management. Its results are read as a gauge of American borrowers and of the health of Wall Street dealmaking.
stocks:JPM.recent: Fed officials questioned JPMorgan, alongside Wells Fargo, Barclays and Morgan Stanley, in a review prompted by worries over private credit. The questions concern what banks have lent to that market, a line of business the largest lenders have built up.

stocks:WFC.standing: One of the four largest US banks, earning most of its income from lending to American households and mid-sized businesses rather than from trading. Its profit moves with interest rates and with how many borrowers fall behind.
stocks:WFC.recent: Fed officials questioned the bank, alongside JPMorgan, Barclays and Morgan Stanley, in a review spurred by worries over private credit. That questioning surfaced only after the share had already fallen, and nothing else reported in the window accounts for the slide.

stocks:BCS.standing: A London-based bank that pairs a British high-street lender and card business with one of the few large investment banks left in Europe. Its earnings swing with trading and deal-making more than those of its domestic rivals.
stocks:BCS.recent: Fed officials questioned Barclays, alongside JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley, in a review prompted by worries over private credit, the lending that banks finance outside public markets. The questioning is new, and nothing reported earlier accounts for the slide that preceded it.

stocks:MS.standing: A Wall Street bank that earns its money managing wealth for individuals and institutions, and from investment banking and trading. Its share price follows deal-making, market activity and the fees on the assets clients keep with it.
stocks:MS.recent: Fed officials questioned Morgan Stanley, along with JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and Barclays, in a review spurred by worries about private credit. The questions were reported after the share had already fallen, and nothing else published in the window accounts for the slide.

poly-will-the-iranian-regime-fall-by-the.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Islamic Republic's government loses power in Iran before the deadline. The price is what traders pay for that outcome, and it moves on war, protest and succession inside the state.
poly-will-the-iranian-regime-fall-by-the.recent: Tehran spent the window behaving like a government that expects to stay: it sent Washington a 7-day plan to end hostilities and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and the US answered through Qatar. At home it executed two men over the killing of police officers during the unrest early this year and says it blocked Starlink during the war.

stocks:RTX.standing: An American aerospace and defence group that owns Pratt & Whitney jet engines, Collins Aerospace and the Raytheon missile business, maker of the Patriot. Its share moves on Pentagon and allied arms budgets and on airline demand.
stocks:RTX.recent: The Royal Australian Air Force made the first release of the HACM, the US hypersonic cruise missile, bringing the weapon to flight test. That is a milestone for a programme in the company's missile business, and it does not account for the fall in the share.

stocks:CME.standing: The Chicago company that runs the CME, CBOT, NYMEX and COMEX exchanges, where the benchmark futures on interest rates, oil, grain and gold trade. It earns a fee on each contract, so its income rises when markets turn volatile.

poly-will-luca-niculescu-be-the-next-pri.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Luca Niculescu, a Romanian diplomat and former journalist, becomes Romania's next prime minister. The price is what traders pay for a share that settles at 100 if he takes the post.

stocks:AVGO.standing: A US chip designer that sells custom processors and networking silicon to the largest data-centre operators, alongside a big infrastructure-software business. Its orders show how much the cloud giants are spending on computing capacity.

stocks:XOM.standing: The largest oil and gas company in the United States, pumping crude and gas from Texas to Guyana and refining it into fuel and chemicals. Its profit follows the oil price, so the share is a reading on what crude earns.

stocks:SU.standing: Canada's largest oil sands producer, based in Calgary. It mines and upgrades bitumen in northern Alberta, refines it, and sells fuel through Petro-Canada stations, so its share moves with the crude price and with its own running costs.
stocks:SU.recent: The Supreme Court in Washington heard the oil industry's bid to end 24-plus climate suits, a case that decides whether producers face those damage claims at all. The hearing came at the very end of the window, and nothing else in the fortnight's news bears on the company's own business or accounts for its share price.

stocks:IT.standing: A research and advisory firm in Stamford, Connecticut, that sells subscriptions to its technology and business analysis to executives. Its rankings of software vendors shape what large companies buy, and its sales track corporate IT budgets.

stocks:J.standing: A Dallas-based engineering and consulting firm that designs and manages water systems, transport networks, data centres and factories. Its revenue follows what governments and large companies commit to building.

stocks:KBR.standing: A Houston engineering and technology contractor that sells mission support, science and logistics staff to governments, chiefly US defence and space agencies. Its revenue rises and falls with what those agencies choose to outsource.
stocks:KBR.recent: NASA is hiring 7,500 contractors as civil servants, reversing the outsourcing that supplies this kind of firm with its government work. That decision was reported after the share had already fallen, and nothing else in the fortnight accounts for the slide.

stocks:NFLX.standing: The world's largest subscription video streaming service, selling monthly plans and advertising in almost every country. Its share price moves on how fast revenue grows, and it sets the pace the Hollywood studios' own services are judged by.

poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-texas-se.standing: What traders on Polymarket pay for a contract that settles in full if a Democrat wins the 2026 US Senate race in Texas. The state has not elected a Democrat to statewide office since 1994, so the seat tests how far the map can move.
poly-will-the-democrats-win-the-texas-se.recent: The fortnight's news touched the venue, not the race. New York sued Polymarket as an illegal gambling operation that lets 18-to-20-year-olds bet where state law sets 21, and an appeals court ruled that states can regulate Kalshi's sports contracts. Neither accounts for what traders are paying on Texas.

poly-will-openai-announce-another-millen.standing: A bet on whether an OpenAI model solves another Millennium Prize Problem by the end of 2026. The Clay Mathematics Institute put $1 million on each of seven such problems, among the hardest open questions in mathematics.

poly-will-the-ecb-announce-a-25-bps-incr.standing: What traders will pay for a contract that pays out if the European Central Bank raises its key interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point at a single meeting. That rate sets the cost of borrowing across the euro area.

poly-will-ukraine-target-moscow-on-octob.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Ukraine strikes Moscow on one named day. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with the tempo of the long-range drone war and with any talk of a strike truce.
poly-will-ukraine-target-moscow-on-octob.recent: Bets on a repeat followed the overnight attack that Moscow's mayor, Sergei Sobyanin, put at 650 drones, which killed two people and set a warehouse on fire. It came days after Zelenskyy offered trilateral talks and India discussed non-attack steps with both sides; nothing reported accounts for the fall that followed.

stocks:GS.standing: A Wall Street investment bank that earns its money advising on mergers, underwriting share and bond sales, trading for clients and managing wealth. Its profits rise and fall with deal-making and market activity, so its share is read as a gauge of both.

stocks:ACN.standing: One of the world's largest consulting and IT outsourcing firms, domiciled in Dublin and listed in New York. Big companies and governments hire it to run technology projects, so its bookings are read as a gauge of corporate tech spending.

poly-will-aleksandar-vucic-united-serbia.standing: What traders will pay for the outcome that Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party takes the most seats in Serbia's parliamentary election. The party has governed since 2012, so the price tracks its hold on power.

poly-will-dallas-cowboys-win-the-2026-nf.standing: A contract that pays out if the Dallas Cowboys finish first in the NFC East, the NFL division they share with Philadelphia, Washington and the New York Giants. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with each week's results.
poly-will-dallas-cowboys-win-the-2026-nf.recent: The news in this window was about the venue, not the team. New York sued Polymarket over allegations of illegal gambling, and an appeals court ruled that Kalshi's sports contracts are subject to state regulations. Neither accounts for the change in what traders will pay for Dallas.

stocks:CEG.standing: The largest operator of nuclear power plants in the United States, split from Exelon in 2022. It sells electricity on long contracts, increasingly to data-centre owners, so its share moves with what buyers will pay for steady carbon-free power.
stocks:CEG.recent: Google signed up as the buyer for 890 megawatts of new nuclear output in the United States, and the deal sent fresh money into nuclear stocks as a group. A technology company committing to reactor power on that scale is the demand these shares are priced on.

poly-will-mojtaba-khamenei-be-head-of-st.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Mojtaba Khamenei is Iran's head of state in 2026. The supreme leader commands the armed forces and has the last word on war and nuclear talks, so it prices who holds that power.
poly-will-mojtaba-khamenei-be-head-of-st.recent: The fortnight's news on Iran was about the war around it: mediation with the US deadlocked, and the Pentagon was reported to be drafting strike options before 3 November. None of it concerned who leads in Tehran, and nothing in it accounts for the change in what traders pay.

stocks:2357.TW.standing: A Taiwanese maker of laptops, motherboards, graphics cards, routers and servers, listed in Taipei. Its sales follow the PC replacement cycle and, increasingly, demand for the servers that run AI models.

stocks:NTGR.standing: A San Jose company that makes Wi-Fi routers, mesh systems and network switches for homes and small businesses. It is one of the few American names in a consumer router market largely supplied by Chinese-founded rivals.

poly-will-mykola-kuleba-win-the-nobel-pe.standing: A contract that pays out if Dmytro Kuleba, Ukraine's former foreign minister, is awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. The price is what traders pay for that outcome; the Norwegian Nobel Committee deliberates in secret, so it moves on rumour.

stocks:ADBE.standing: The maker of Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere and Acrobat, the standard tools of designers and video editors, sold by subscription. Its share is a bet on whether AI image tools replace that software or get sold inside it.
stocks:ADBE.recent: An AI developer released seven free apps that copy Photoshop, Illustrator and Premiere, the programs Adobe charges a subscription for. They arrived after the share had already fallen, so they do not account for the slide, and nothing else in the fortnight's news does.

poly-will-alberto-nunez-feijoo-be-the-ne.standing: What traders pay for the outcome that Alberto Núñez Feijóo, leader of Spain's conservative People's Party, is the next prime minister. Spanish governments are built in parliament, so winning the most seats does not settle it.

stocks:ARGX.standing: A Dutch-registered biotechnology company listed in Brussels and on Nasdaq. Nearly all its sales come from one antibody-clearing drug for autoimmune diseases, so each trial in a new condition moves the share.
stocks:ARGX.recent: Vyvgart did no better than placebo in a Phase 3 trial in Sjögren's disease, a chronic autoimmune condition with no approved disease-modifying treatment. The drug blocks the FcRn receptor so the body clears IgG antibodies faster, and a clean failure raises the question of whether those antibodies drive Sjögren's at all.

stocks:DAL.standing: One of the three largest US airlines, flying from hubs including Atlanta, Detroit and Minneapolis. Its share price moves on jet fuel costs and on demand for business and premium travel, and it reports results before its rivals.

stocks:INFY.standing: An Indian company based in Bengaluru that writes and runs software for banks, retailers and manufacturers abroad. Most of its revenue comes from North America, so US spending and US work-visa rules reach it directly.

stocks:WIT.standing: One of India's largest IT services firms, based in Bengaluru, writing and running software for banks, retailers and manufacturers abroad. Most of its revenue comes from US and European clients, so it moves on their tech budgets.

poly-saudi-arabia-military-action-agains.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Saudi Arabia carries out military action on Yemeni territory before the deadline. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on each strike across the border.
poly-saudi-arabia-military-action-agains.recent: Traders paid more after the Houthis hit two Saudi airports, injuring three in Jazan, and warned that Saudi airspace would become a theatre of operations. The Mecca alliance activated collective deterrence, with Pakistan and Turkey to deploy troops to Saudi Arabia, and the Trump administration backed the kingdom's right to defend itself.

stocks:CTSH.standing: A New Jersey-based IT services firm that builds and runs software for banks, insurers and hospitals, with most of its staff in India. It is among the largest users of US work visas, so immigration rules hit its costs.

stocks:DJT.standing: The company behind Truth Social, the social network Donald Trump posts on, listed on Nasdaq under the ticker DJT. Trump is its majority owner, and the share trades on his political fortunes far more than on its small revenue.
stocks:DJT.recent: A judge in Washington is weighing whether Trump can charge for early access to his Truth Social posts, where instant access costs up to $100,000 monthly. The case puts a revenue line of the platform in question, but it arrived at the end of the window and does not account for the slide that came before it.
